clue.text: Make introduction before stroll

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
to amble is to stroll

explanation.surface: Someone introduces themselves before going for a leisurely walk.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is used here as a verb: to make a preliminary statement.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, the word means to give an opening statement or introductory remarks before the main matter.

clue.text: Beret in Algeciras protects light-sensitive tissue

indicators.note: protects means these words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A hat worn in a Spanish port shields the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: The layer at the back of the eye that responds to light is this tissue.

clue.text: Assistant holds last of talks in private

indicators.note: holds means the word for assistant wraps around the next letter

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of talks

explanation.surface: A helper keeps the end of the negotiations confidential.
explanation.definitionFit: Something said aside is said privately, out of others' hearing.

clue.text: Cat is able to swim about in watery expanse

indicators.note: swim about suggests the letters moving around into a new order

explanation.surface: A cat is capable of swimming around in a large body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: This northern European sea is a large expanse of water.

clue.text: Nobleman seizing power starts to use gun silencer

indicators.note: seizing means the nobleman's title grabs a letter inside it

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A lord takes control and begins to fire a gun with a muffler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silencer' suggests a gun attachment, but the answer silences sound for the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug worn in the ear blocks out noise, so it acts as a silencer.

clue.text: Tax officer reportedly chooses subject matter

parts.note: TO is the abbreviation for tax officer

indicators.note: reportedly says we want a word that sounds like the synonym, not its spelling

parts.note: chooses means picks

explanation.surface: A tax inspector, it is said, gets to pick what is discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: Themes or matters under discussion are the subjects of talk, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Jazz pianist gives thanks to pot

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
a pot is a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A jazz musician expresses gratitude to a cooking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Tatum was a celebrated American jazz pianist.

clue.text: Soldier's truck carrying church canopy

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier
a ute is a utility truck

explanation.surface: A soldier's lorry carries a church's awning.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabric canopy that slows a jumper's fall from an aircraft.

clue.text: Prisoner's accommodation with electronic fuse

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
a flat is accommodation
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A convict's home has an electric fuse box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuse' looks like an electrical noun but is the verb, meaning to merge.
explanation.definitionFit: To conflate is to merge two things into one, as to fuse them.

clue.text: A test of the heart cavities

parts.note: a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A medical examination of the chambers of the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The atria are the upper chambers of the heart, so the adjective describes something relating to them.

clue.text: Shy about dressing in old-fashioned way

parts.note: re means about or concerning
tiring is an archaic word for attiring or dressing

explanation.surface: A bashful person wears dated clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: TIRING here has nothing to do with fatigue: it is an old shortening of attiring.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved, bashful person is described as retiring, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Refusing to accept the truth, I lie and foolishly will conceal name

indicators.note: will conceal means the rearranged letters wrap around another letter
foolishly suggests the letters of these words are jumbled into a silly order

explanation.surface: A liar who foolishly keeps someone's name secret will not face facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' scrambles I LIE AND into INDEIAL, and 'will conceal' places N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in denial is the idiom for refusing to admit an unpleasant reality.

clue.text: Spot a copper lurking in motorway lane half-cut

indicators.note: lurking in means hiding inside the other pieces

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: half-cut means only the first half of the word lane is kept

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer hides in a motorway lane, drunk, and is spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it trims lane to LA.
explanation.definitionFit: A macula is a spot or patch, especially a discoloured mark on the skin or the area of the retina.

clue.text: Research student stated group that's gone wrong should accept answer

indicators.note: should accept means the rearranged letters take in another letter
gone wrong says these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A doctoral researcher reports a failed group project and must face up to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's gone wrong' scrambles STATED GROUP; 'should accept' adds A within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone studying for a higher degree after a first one is often doing research.

clue.text: Flavour of Ulster sausage

parts.note: pepper is a flavouring
o' is a short form of of, as in o'clock
NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster

explanation.surface: A sausage with a Northern Irish taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy Italian-American dried sausage.

clue.text: Sceptics assign OT rhetoric ultimately for analysis

indicators.note: for analysis suggests the letters being broken down and reassembled
ultimately picks the final letter of rhetoric

explanation.surface: Doubters hand Old Testament rhetoric over to be scrutinised.
explanation.walkthrough: OT is the Old Testament; 'ultimately' gives C from rhetoric, and 'for analysis' scrambles ASSIGNOT with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnostics doubt that God's existence can be known, so they are religious sceptics.

clue.text: Missing in action after getting to unknown A&E with blood poisoning

indicators.note: after places missing in action following the other pieces

parts.note: X is an unknown in algebra
A&E is the accident and emergency department, written AE
MIA is missing in action

explanation.surface: A soldier missing in action reaches casualty with poisoned blood.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: Toxaemia is the presence of bacterial toxins in the blood, a form of poisoning.

clue.text: To express disapproval about South American church shows excessive desire to please

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the next piece

parts.note: to complain is to express disapproval
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Grumbling about a South American church reveals a fawning eagerness to please.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaisance is an obliging, overly willing readiness to go along with others' wishes.

clue.text: They crack the case for Rebus

definitions.text: They crack the case for Rebus

parts.note: to crack a puzzle is to solve it

indicators.note: the case for means the outside letters of Rebus are taken

explanation.surface: Detectives solve the mystery for Ian Rankin's Inspector Rebus.
explanation.walkthrough: Rebus is Ian Rankin's Edinburgh detective, but a rebus is also a picture puzzle, which these people crack.
explanation.definitionFit: People who work out puzzles or mysteries are those who crack them.

clue.text: Wilde's awards

definitions.meaning: belonging to the writer Oscar Wilde, read with an apostrophe
the Academy Awards for film are given as statuettes with this nickname

explanation.surface: The prizes won by the playwright Wilde.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessive of Wilde's first name, and also the film industry's Academy Award statuettes.

clue.text: Special gift of story books

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A book of stories as a special present.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural aptitude or flair for something is described as a gift.

clue.text: Part of heath in estate that was once yours

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of heathland on an estate used to belong to you.
explanation.definitionFit: Thine is the archaic possessive form meaning yours, no longer in everyday use.

clue.text: Call for those retiring to carry on with Royal Mail

parts.note: to last is to carry on or continue
the Royal Mail is the British postal service, so post

explanation.surface: Pensioners are told to keep going with their postal work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'those retiring' suggests pensioners but means soldiers going to bed; the call is the bugle signal at the day's end, also played at remembrance ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: This military bugle call signals the end of the day, when troops retire for the night.

clue.text: Former currency adopts European coin

indicators.note: adopts means the old currency takes in the next letter

parts.note: the pice was a former Indian coin

explanation.surface: An obsolete currency takes on a European coin, like the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a coin, as in a fifty-pence piece.

clue.text: Prince quits pantomime when dressed as a marine fossil!

indicators.note: dressed suggests the remaining letters are dressed up in a new arrangement
quits means the letter for prince leaves the word

explanation.surface: A prince leaves a pantomime dressed up as a sea fossil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quits' takes P out of PANTOMIME to leave ANTOMIME, which 'dressed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammonites are the coiled shells of extinct sea molluscs, found as fossils.

clue.text: One's cold joining march back from frozen peak

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is read as is, a link
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: back means the word for march is read backwards

parts.note: to pace is to march

explanation.surface: Someone with a cold joins a march back from a snowy mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent covering of ice on a mountain top or polar region forms a frozen summit.

clue.text: Case appointment is around four

indicators.note: is around means the first word surrounds the next piece

parts.note: a date is an appointment
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A meeting has been arranged for about four o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the dative is a case, marking the indirect object.

clue.text: Small American coins reportedly causing uncertainty

parts.note: US means American

indicators.note: reportedly says we want a word that sounds like the synonym, not its spelling

parts.note: pence are British coins

explanation.surface: Rumours about small US coins create doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious uncertainty about what will happen is a synonym for the state of being kept waiting.
